study_identification_part.si4_title: Molecular and micro-architectural mapping of gray matter alterations in psychosis

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To characterize the molecular and micro-architectural attributes underlying patterns of cortical atypical maturation in different psychosis-related groups by computing centiles from regional volumes and mapping 46 neurobiological features to identify vulnerability factors associated with abnormal brain development across the psychosis spectrum.

For example, a subject at the 20th centile would have a volume that is 'approximately' lower than 80% of individuals of the same age and sex after adjusting for scanning site offset... clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Wilcoxon rank-sum test with FDR correction for regional centile differences between diagnostic groups and HC; Cohen's d effect sizes computed between regional centiles for each pair of groups; permutation tests (10,000 permutations) with FDR correction to assess significance of effect sizes and SSD; PCA-CCA multivariate modeling to map neurobiological features to centiles; spin test (spatial autocorrelation-preserving permutation) for statistical significance of PCA-CCA models; bootstrap sampling (1000 samples) to estimate standard errors of model weights; Pearson correlation to compute loadings (contribution of each neurobiological feature to predicted centiles); sensitivity analyses including global centile correction, Euler index correction, leave-one-study-out cross-validation, and parcellation comparison (Schaefer 400 vs DK); neurobiological similarity matrix correlated with structural co-vulnerability matrix to identify associations between regions with similar neurobiological attributes and overlapping structural vulnerability profiles
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: All psychosis-related groups showed significantly decreased global and regional GM volume centiles compared to HC, with greater impact on clinically diagnosed groups (FEP and chronic); neurobiological features (especially metabolism, neurotransmitters, and synapse density) were highly co-localized with abnormal GM trajectories, supporting the regional vulnerability hypothesis.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Significantly decreased centile scores in global GM volume were found across all psychosis-related groups (relatives P=0.0021; PE P=0.0124; FEP P<10^-7; chronic P<10^-28). The number of significantly affected regions increased with disorder severity, supporting a continuum view of psychosis. FEP patients showed significant centile reductions in all regions except inferior temporal and temporal pole, while chronic SCZ showed reductions in all regions. Relatives showed reductions in association cortices, particularly cingulate, temporal, and frontal regions. PE groups showed heterogeneous patterns, with only PE-clinical individuals showing 11 significantly reduced regions. Between-group comparisons revealed that the chronic group exhibited decreased centiles in frontal and temporal lobes compared to relatives, PE, and FEP, but showed increases in occipital lobe compared to FEP. PCA-CCA models revealed significant associations between neurobiological features and centiles for all groups except PE (r=0.63 for FEP, r=0.68 for chronic). The greatest negative loadings (indicating high presence of features in regions with low centiles) included neurotransmitters (5-HT1B, 5-HT2A, α4β2, NET, GABA), synapse density, excitatory neurons, and metabolism (CMRGlu, CBF, CMRO2). Positive loadings (indicating low presence in affected regions) included neurotransmitters (5-HT1A, D2, DAT), astrocytes, OPC, microglia, and Layer III. The chronic group mainly exhibited negative loadings, indicating generalized presence of features in regions with decreased centiles. Neurobiological similarity was significantly associated with structural co-vulnerability to psychosis (r=0.21, P<10^-6), indicating that regions with similar neurobiological attributes tend to exhibit overlapping structural vulnerability profiles across the psychosis spectrum.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Heterogeneous groups with varying sample sizes and diagnoses; antipsychotic medication may impact cortical volume in chronic patients; normative models only available for hemisphere-averaged volumes (not subcortical, cortical thickness, or surface area); risk of overfitting in PCA-CCA with limited sample size (34 regions); neurobiological data derived from normative non-psychotic individuals rather than patients with psychosis
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, psychotic disorders were grouped with varying sample sizes and diagnoses, resulting in heterogeneous groups... Second, while abnormalities in relatives, PE, and FEP individuals are not influenced by medication, antipsychotic drugs may be impacting cortical volume in chronic individuals [74]. Third, since computing the normative trajectories requires hundreds of thousands of CPU hours, the models provided by Bethlehem et al. [20] were only available for cortical brain volume averaged across hemispheres (not subcortical volume, cortical thickness, or surface area). Fourth, although in this limited sample size scenario (34 regions) the CCA multivariate approach has a risk of overfitting [75], we first applied PCA before CCA to prevent this issue, and then performed a PLS to confirm the results. Fifth, neurobiological data used here were derived from normative non-psychotic individuals. Future work with a neurobiological atlas of individuals with schizophrenia could provide new insights into the molecular alterations causally associated with abnormal brain alterations.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: PCA dimensionality reduction was performed before CCA to prevent overfitting, with explained variance tested at 60%, 70%, 80%, and 90%; the model with lowest explained variance that was significant according to spin test was selected; PLS analysis was performed as sensitivity test and showed high correlation (r>0.92) with PCA-CCA loadings; leave-one-study-out cross-validation demonstrated robustness of centiles and loadings within chronic group and SCZ diagnosis; sensitivity analyses showed results were robust to global centile correction, Euler index correction, and different parcellation schemes (DK vs Schaefer 400); loadings were reported instead of weights to better represent the extent to which each feature contributed to the model, though both showed high resemblance

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study represents a comprehensive application of pre-trained normative models to the psychosis spectrum. The study included 1256 psychosis-related individuals across 8 diagnoses and 38,696 healthy controls from 8 major datasets. A unique aspect is the multivariate mapping of 46 neurobiological features (neurotransmitters, cell types, layer thickness, microstructure, cortical expansion, metabolism) to identify vulnerability factors underlying atypical brain maturation. The normative model from Bethlehem et al. 2022 was trained on approximately 120,000 participants from 100 studies spanning the entire lifespan (17 post-conception weeks to 100 years). MRI data were acquired on different scanners (1.5-3T) with varying protocols across sites. Scanning for FEP patients was performed prior to initiation of antipsychotic medication. The study used hemisphere-averaged regional volumes (34 DK regions) because the pre-trained model only provided hemisphere-averaged normative trajectories. All code is available at https://github.com/RafaelRomeroGarcia/NeurobiologyCentilesPsychosis.
